page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is a virtual server in the High Performance lineup, offering a balanced general-purpose resource profile. It provides 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz, supporting hyperthreading with two threads per core. Memory capacity is 12.0 GB, allocating 3.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, 32 KB of L1 data cache, and vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI. Local storage is bundled as a 260 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete GPU acceleration is present.

Benchmark results show balanced middle-tier single-core efficiency but constrained multi-core throughput due to its shared 2-core physical topology. Single-threaded tests such as Geekbench single-core (1165.0), stress-ng single-core (1466.08), and gzip compression (24.18 GB/sec) fall within the middle 50% category. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads indicate lower performance bounds, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 3734.0, PassMark CPU scoring 6551.68, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression dropping into the bottom 10% (17.19 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth is healthy for cached reads at 421.33 GB/sec and uncached writes at 28.11 GB/sec, though uncached large-block reads are limited to 36.96 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is centered on providing a capable local NVMe storage volume paired with moderate memory density for shared virtual computing. The architecture trade-off lies in the shared dual-core foundation, which restricts dense computational tasks such as large compilation jobs (Geekbench clang score of 5818.0) or heavy database query loads. However, the system delivers solid transactional throughput for caching layers, achieving 6.4 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. The server fits web serving, caching proxies, staging environments, background task queues, and low-concurrency backend services.
description: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is a High Performance series virtual server built on x86_64 Intel Xeon hardware running at 2.0 GHz. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores, 12.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 260 GB NVMe SSD, without dedicated GPU capabilities. Single-core performance sits in the middle 50% across benchmarks like Geekbench (1165.0) and stress-ng (1466.08), supported by AVX-512 vector instruction support and 16 MB of L3 cache. However, multi-core throughput is constrained by the two physical cores, placing multi-threaded tasks like clang compilation and PassMark testing in the bottom 25%. In-memory transaction throughput is stable, yielding 6.4 million Redis SET operations per second. This instance fits general web application serving, Redis caching nodes, microservices, and lightweight development workloads.
